subject: Follow-up: Context length & pricing profile for Acme (token volumes)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Context length & pricing profile for Acme (token volumes)

Hi Samir —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from today's discovery so we can size pricing and match the right context-length plan: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + longer context retrieval for agent assist.
- Typical input (prompt) per session: 600–1,200 tokens (avg ~900).
- Average expected completion: 200–800 tokens depending on summary vs. proactive response.
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~150–200 (expected steady-state 80–120).
- Latency SLO: P95 < 300ms for single-turn prompts (important for support UI).
- Security: SOC2 + VPC requirements noted (we'll loop in Solutions).

What we need from you to finalize a pricing range:
1) Typical prompt + completion token distributions (avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens). If you have sample logs or a small export that'd be ideal.
2) Expected monthly token volume (or ranges: conservative/expected/optimistic).
3) Any 8k/32k/128k context needs: e.g., how often do you require >8k tokens? Occasional (0–1%)/regular (5–10%)/core (30%+).

Next steps I propose:
- You: share a short token sample CSV (columns: session_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens).
- Us: I'll run a quick profile and send back a cost estimate showing $/1M-token unit economics across model/context-tier (8k/32k/128k) and a recommended plan (hosted vs. dedicated).

If you prefer, we can do a 20-minute follow-up demo of the profiling tool — Jordan is copied and can join.

Thanks,

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ava Johnson <ava.j@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Context length & pricing profile for Acme (token volumes)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A couple quick answers and I've attached a small export (acme_pricing_sample_tokens.csv) with a week's worth of anonymized session token counts. High-level:

- Avg prompt tokens: 920
- Avg completion tokens: 410
- Median prompt: 850; Median completion: 320
- Monthly active sessions estimate (current): 140k sessions/month across support/agent-assist (we expect 2–3x growth over 12 months).
- Token volume estimate: current ~85M tokens/month; expected ~200–250M tokens/month in 12 months.

Context length: most sessions are under 8k, but we have two flavors:
- Short dialogs (80%): prompt+history < 2k tokens, completions < 400 tokens.
- Long retrievals (20%): we stitch multiple docs and can hit 12k–40k in the prompt occasionally — maybe 3–5% exceed 32k; very rare >128k.

Budget: at the moment we have a target blended unit cost of roughly $1,800–$2,500 per 1M tokens (this is a broad internal target across model tiers, but we can be flexible if Redwood can show unit economics and performance tradeoffs).

Happy to have Jordan and Ava on a call if that helps. Next step for us: see your profiling results + recommended plan and an indicative quote.

—Samir
Samir Patel | Head of Product, AI
Acme Corp
samir.patel@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Context length & pricing profile for Acme (token volumes)

Hi Samir — thanks for the CSV and the high-level numbers, super helpful. I profiled the sample and put together an indicative unit economics run (attached: redwood_pricing_quote_v1.pdf). Highlights below — these are illustrative and we can tighten with a longer sample: 

Token profile (from sample):
- Avg prompt: 915 tokens (close to your 920)
- Avg completion: 405 tokens
- Avg total tokens per session: ~1,320 tokens

Monthly volume scenarios (tokens/month):
- Current: 85M
- 12mo forecast: 225M (midpoint of your 200–250M)

Indicative $/1M-token unit economics (hosted catalog models / example):
- 8k context model (recommended for ~80% of sessions): $2,300 / 1M tokens (includes auto-batching & prefix cache savings)
- 32k context model (for the 17% of sessions that need up to ~32k): $3,400 / 1M tokens
- 128k context model (reserved for the rare heavy retrievals ~3%): $12,000 / 1M tokens (high resource cost; consider targeted routing or hybrid approach)

Notes and recommendations:
- Because only ~3–5% of requests exceed 32k, we recommend routing those to a dedicated/spot pool with targeted batching to reduce tail cost.
- For your 12mo forecast volume, a committed Dedicated plan reduces unit cost by ~20–35% depending on commit level and burst policy; I'll include dedicated pricing in the full quote.
- We can also apply KV-prefix caching for repeated context chunks (saves ~10–20% on token bill for retrieval-heavy flows).

Questions for you to confirm:
1) Are the 3–5% >32k requests business-critical (need same latency/SLO) or can they be processed as lower-priority batch jobs?
2) Do you have a preference for hosted vs. dedicated long-term? If you need an SLA and consistent latency, Dedicated looks attractive at your forecasted volume.

Next steps:
- I'll send a short comparison table (hosted vs. dedicated) with committed tiers and estimated monthly spend at current vs. forecast volume.
- If it's useful, Jordan can run a quick demo of routing rules (can show how we offload >32k to a cheaper path).

Would you be available for a 20-30 minute sync Tuesday or Wednesday next week?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Marissa — thanks, I reviewed the quote and the numbers look reasonable as a starting point. A few quick clarifications before we pull this into procurement: 

- Can you show blended estimates at our forecasted 225M tokens/month for hosted vs dedicated (ballpark committed tiers)?
- For the 128k tier: can you confirm if that price assumes dedicated-only or if hosted supports it on-demand?
- Any recommended guardrails to keep the 128k calls down (e.g., token caps, autoprompts to summarize/split)?

We're aiming to present an internal business case by next Friday — if you can get the hosted vs dedicated monthly spend table and the routing/guardrail suggestions by Wednesday that would be ideal.

I'll also upload a more representative month of logs (replace the sample) once I have procurement lined up so you can run the detailed profile.

Thanks — Samir
